item.content:encoded:
The Greater Washington Partnership (GWP) is inviting applications for its Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship, offering an exciting opportunity for students and recent graduates who are passionate about economic development, entrepreneurship, regional growth, innovation, and public-private collaboration. This paid internship places successful applicants at the center of one of the United States’ most influential regional economic organizations, where they will contribute to initiatives that shape the future of the Greater Washington metropolitan region.

The internship provides participants with meaningful professional experience by allowing them to work alongside policy experts, business leaders, government officials, nonprofit organizations, and economic development professionals. Interns will contribute to research, stakeholder engagement, event coordination, and strategic initiatives designed to strengthen economic competitiveness across Maryland, Virginia, and Washington, DC.

If you are looking for an internship that combines research, policy, business strategy, entrepreneurship, and regional development, this opportunity offers an outstanding platform to gain practical experience while building valuable professional networks.

About Greater Washington Partnership

The Greater Washington Partnership is a unique nonprofit alliance that brings together many of the most influential employers throughout the Greater Washington region, spanning Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia.

Unlike traditional nonprofit organizations, the Partnership serves as a bridge between the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. It convenes leaders from business, government, education, and community organizations to solve regional challenges and promote sustainable economic growth.

Its mission focuses on addressing critical issues including:

  • Skills and workforce development
  • Talent attraction and retention
  • Regional transportation and mobility
  • Infrastructure development
  • Inclusive economic growth
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Innovation
  • Business competitiveness

The Partnership envisions transforming the corridor stretching from Baltimore to Richmond into one of the world’s most competitive, prosperous, and attractive places to live, work, invest, and build businesses.

About the Economic Growth Internship

The Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship is designed for individuals interested in understanding how regional economies grow and how cross-sector partnerships influence public policy, innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic opportunity.

The internship supports implementation of the organization’s Region Rising Report, a strategic roadmap released in 2026 that outlines priorities for creating a stronger and more resilient regional economy.

Interns will become active contributors to projects that advance these priorities through research, stakeholder engagement, innovation programming, and policy support.

Rather than observing from the sidelines, interns become part of the Economic Growth team, contributing ideas and supporting projects that directly influence regional development initiatives.

Internship Responsibilities

Selected interns will participate in a broad range of professional activities, including:

1. Research and Policy Analysis

Interns will conduct detailed research across several important policy and economic topics, including:

  • Regional economic development
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Procurement
  • Affordable housing
  • Financial inclusion
  • Innovation ecosystems
  • Business competitiveness

They will also analyze findings and prepare concise reports that help guide strategic decision-making.

2. Stakeholder Engagement

Interns will help coordinate collaboration among numerous stakeholders by:

  • Scheduling meetings
  • Preparing meeting agendas
  • Developing briefing materials
  • Recording meeting notes
  • Tracking follow-up actions
  • Supporting ongoing communication

This exposure provides firsthand experience in managing relationships across multiple sectors.

3. Supporting the Region Rising Initiative

The internship directly supports implementation of the Partnership’s Region Rising Report.

Interns will assist with:

  • Research supporting report initiatives
  • Monitoring progress
  • Gathering economic insights
  • Supporting strategic projects
  • Coordinating implementation activities

4. Entrepreneurship and Innovation Programs

Interns will contribute to programs that promote innovation throughout the region.

This includes supporting the Partnership’s Next Level Accelerator, which works with entrepreneurs and startup ecosystems.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Assisting with entrepreneur engagement
  • Supporting accelerator programming
  • Researching innovation trends
  • Helping organize entrepreneurship initiatives

5. Event Planning and Coordination

Interns will work with several internal departments to support events and public engagement.

Tasks may include:

  • Coordinating logistics
  • Preparing event materials
  • Communicating with speakers
  • Supporting registrations
  • Assisting during live events
  • Helping with post-event follow-up

6. Cross-Functional Collaboration

Interns will collaborate with various organizational teams including:

  • Marketing
  • Communications
  • Public Policy
  • Business Development
  • Events
  • Economic Growth

This interdisciplinary exposure allows interns to understand how nonprofit organizations coordinate large-scale regional initiatives.

7. Strategic Thinking

Rather than simply completing administrative tasks, interns are encouraged to contribute ideas and serve as thought partners on improving the Partnership’s economic growth initiatives.

Internship Benefits

Participants can expect numerous professional benefits, including:

  • Paid internship at $20 per hour
  • Practical experience in economic development
  • Exposure to regional policy development
  • Networking with business and government leaders
  • Experience working within a leading nonprofit organization
  • Professional mentorship
  • Research and analytical experience
  • Event management experience
  • Collaboration across multiple sectors
  • Enhanced communication and leadership skills
  • Strong resume-building experience
  • Exposure to entrepreneurship ecosystems

Internship Schedule

The internship is expected to begin:

  • End of August 2026
  • Early September 2026

Work schedule:

  • Tuesdays
  • Wednesdays
  • Thursdays

Expected weekly commitment:

  • 25–29 hours per week

Internship Location

Washington, DC

The Partnership’s office is:

  • Located south of Dupont Circle
  • Accessible by Metro
  • Positioned within one of the nation’s leading policy and business hubs

Compensation

Selected interns will receive:

  • $20 per hour

This makes the internship both professionally rewarding and financially beneficial for students and recent graduates.

Required Qualifications

Applicants should meet the following requirements:

  • Currently enrolled as a junior or senior undergraduate student
  • OR enrolled in a postgraduate program
  • OR be a recent graduate
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Strong verbal communication skills
  • Excellent presentation skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Experience using Microsoft Excel
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Word
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment
  • Strong organizational abilities
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments simultaneously
  • Comfortable working with evolving priorities
  • Team-oriented mindset
  • Curiosity about regional economic growth
  • Interest in cross-sector collaboration

Preferred Qualifications

Although not mandatory, the following qualifications will strengthen an application:

  • Previous internship experience
  • Work-based learning experience
  • Interest in entrepreneurship
  • Interest in procurement
  • Interest in affordable housing
  • Interest in financial inclusion
  • Data analysis experience
  • Data visualization skills
  • Creative problem-solving ability
  • Resourcefulness
  • Familiarity with the Baltimore-to-Richmond region
  • Event coordination experience

Why This Internship Stands Out

Many internships focus narrowly on administrative work.

This internship offers significantly broader exposure by allowing participants to contribute to:

  • Public-private partnerships
  • Economic research
  • Entrepreneurship ecosystems
  • Regional competitiveness
  • Policy development
  • Innovation strategy
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Economic inclusion

Participants gain insight into how large-scale economic initiatives are developed and implemented while building relationships with influential leaders from multiple sectors.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is ideal for students and recent graduates interested in careers involving:

  • Economic development
  • Public policy
  • Urban planning
  • Government relations
  • Public administration
  • Business strategy
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Economic research
  • Consulting
  • Nonprofit leadership
  • Regional planning
  • Innovation management

                                                             APPLY HERE

Important Information

  • Organization: Greater Washington Partnership
  • Position: Economic Growth Intern
  • Location: Washington, DC
  • Internship Type: Paid
  • Work Schedule: Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays
  • Hours Per Week: 25–29
  • Compensation: $20 per hour
  • Start Date: End of August/Early September 2026
  • Visa Sponsorship: Not available
  • Work Authorization: Applicants must already be eligible to work in the United States.

Application Process

Interested candidates should:

  1. Review the Greater Washington Partnership’s mission and recent initiatives.
  2. Explore the organization’s LinkedIn page and media coverage to understand its work.
  3. Prepare an updated resume highlighting relevant education, research, leadership, internship, and communication experience.
  4. Submit their application through the organization’s official application portal.

Application Deadline

No application deadline has been specified in the opportunity announcement. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since internship positions may close once filled.

Conclusion

The Greater Washington Partnership Economic Growth Internship represents an outstanding opportunity for students and recent graduates seeking practical experience in regional economic development, entrepreneurship, policy research, and cross-sector collaboration. Beyond earning competitive hourly compensation, interns will gain valuable exposure to high-level strategic initiatives that shape one of America’s most economically significant regions. Through hands-on involvement in research, stakeholder engagement, innovation programming, and policy implementation, participants will build skills and professional networks that can serve as a strong foundation for future careers in public policy, nonprofit leadership, consulting, business strategy, and economic development. Applicants who are passionate about creating lasting economic impact and contributing to inclusive regional growth should strongly consider applying as soon as possible.

item.content:encoded:
The Center for Global Development is recruiting a Research Analyst in London to support its work with the Smart Buys Alliance, an international collaboration focused on identifying and promoting highly cost-effective development interventions.

This full-time, mid-level position combines empirical research, quantitative analysis, policy writing, project coordination and event support. The successful candidate will help examine how bilateral donors, development agencies and governments use evidence on cost-effectiveness when making funding and policy decisions.

The Research Analyst will be based in London and is expected to work from CGD’s office at least three days each week. The position offers an annual salary of £46,725–£51,187, together with additional benefits.

The role is expected to begin as soon as possible and will initially continue until 29 February 2028. An extension may be possible, depending on the availability of funding.

Applications close on 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM British Summer Time.

CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 Overview

Key details of the opportunity include:

  • Position: Research Analyst
  • Organisation: Center for Global Development
  • Project: Smart Buys Alliance
  • Location: London, United Kingdom
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Career level: Mid-level
  • Salary: £46,725–£51,187 per year, plus benefits
  • Start date: As soon as possible
  • Contract duration: Fixed term until 29 February 2028
  • Extension: Subject to funding availability
  • Posting date: 23 July 2026
  • Application deadline: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST
  • Office requirement: At least three days per week
  • Work-authorisation requirement: Right to live and work in the United Kingdom

About the Center for Global Development

The Center for Global Development, commonly known as CGD, is an independent, non-partisan and nonprofit policy research organisation with offices in Washington, DC, and London.

CGD conducts empirical research on policies, institutions and financial decisions that affect low- and middle-income countries. Its work examines how governments, international organisations, corporations, development agencies and financial institutions can contribute to more inclusive and sustainable development.

The organisation combines research with engagement across the global policy community. Rather than producing analysis solely for academic audiences, CGD seeks to translate research findings into practical recommendations that can influence development policy, financing and implementation.

Its work often sits at the intersection of:

  • Development economics
  • Public policy
  • International finance
  • Aid effectiveness
  • Global institutions
  • Poverty reduction
  • Evidence-based decision-making
  • Development cooperation

The Research Analyst will support this wider mission by contributing to work on how development organisations identify, assess and use evidence about cost-effective interventions.

About the Smart Buys Alliance

The Smart Buys Alliance connects development agencies, philanthropic organisations and research institutions seeking to increase investment in effective development interventions.

The alliance promotes the use of evidence when governments and donors decide how to allocate limited development resources. Its work is particularly concerned with identifying interventions that can produce substantial positive outcomes relative to their costs.

The alliance operates through three principal areas of work.

Developing On-Demand Smart Buy Lists

The Smart Buys Alliance supports the development of lists identifying development interventions with strong evidence of cost-effectiveness.

These resources are intended to help funders and policymakers compare options and direct resources toward programmes that are likely to deliver significant results.

Supporting Implementation and Evidence Building

Identifying an effective intervention is only one part of the process. The alliance also supports implementation and encourages donors to coordinate their efforts to strengthen the evidence base.

This may involve examining how interventions perform in different settings, identifying implementation constraints and understanding whether the results of one programme can be reproduced elsewhere.

Convening a Community of Practice

The alliance brings together policymakers, researchers, funders and development practitioners to exchange evidence, experience and practical lessons.

The Smart Buys Alliance is a collaboration involving:

  • Center for Effective Global Action
  • Cooperation Globale
  • Center for Global Development
  • Global Poverty Research Lab
  • Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab
  • Participating donor agencies and partners

The Research Analyst will support CGD’s contribution to this partnership.

Purpose of the Research Analyst Position

The Research Analyst will provide analytical, operational and administrative support to CGD’s Smart Buys Alliance work.

The role is intended to help the project deliver accurate, timely and policy-relevant research outputs. It is not limited to data analysis: the selected candidate will also contribute to writing, coordination, stakeholder engagement and the organisation of policy events.

The Research Analyst will report to Michelle Rao, Fellow at CGD Europe, and work closely with members of the broader research team.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between detailed analytical work and practical project coordination. On one day, the Analyst may be cleaning a dataset or reviewing causal-inference evidence; on another, they may be revising a policy report, coordinating a roundtable or arranging travel for project partners.

Research and Analytical Responsibilities

Analysing Donor Use of Cost-Effectiveness Evidence

A major component of the role will involve examining how donor agencies engage with and use evidence about cost-effective development interventions.

The Research Analyst may help investigate questions such as:

  • How do donor agencies define cost-effectiveness?
  • What evidence do they use when selecting interventions?
  • How consistently is evidence incorporated into funding decisions?
  • What organisational factors encourage or prevent evidence use?
  • How can the use of cost-effectiveness evidence be monitored?
  • How might donor practices change over time?

Work in this area may include:

  • Literature reviews
  • Data collection
  • Data extraction
  • Dataset construction
  • Data cleaning
  • Quantitative analysis
  • Textual analysis
  • Review of policy and organisational documents

Textual Analysis Using Large Language Models

The position may involve using large language models to support the analysis of textual data.

This could include examining development strategies, policy documents, donor reports or other materials to identify patterns in how organisations discuss and apply evidence.

Candidates with prior experience using large language models for evidence synthesis or textual analysis will have an advantage. However, this experience is identified as beneficial rather than mandatory.

Applicants should understand that the role requires analytical judgement. Tools may assist with large volumes of text, but conclusions must still be transparent, credible and suitable for policy research.

Research on Evidence Use in Development Policy

The Research Analyst will support wider research on how evidence informs international development policy.

This may include:

  • Original data analysis
  • Quantitative research
  • Cost-effectiveness analysis
  • Heterogeneity analysis
  • Causal-inference methods
  • Evidence synthesis
  • Interpretation of empirical findings
  • Preparation of charts and visualisations

Heterogeneity analysis may be used to examine whether an intervention produces different effects across populations, countries or implementation settings.

Cost-effectiveness analysis may involve comparing the costs and outcomes of different interventions to assess which approaches offer greater value.

Drafting Research Outputs

The Research Analyst will contribute to drafting and revising:

  • Academic or policy papers
  • Research reports
  • Policy briefs
  • Blogs
  • Monitoring products
  • Analytical summaries
  • Supporting materials for stakeholders

The selected candidate must be able to communicate technical findings clearly without flattening the nuance out of them. Policy audiences generally need clarity, not a statistical fog bank.

The Analyst will work under the guidance of the Research Fellow and in collaboration with the wider research team.

Monitoring Evidence-Use Initiatives

The role also involves tracking initiatives intended to increase the use of evidence by:

  • Development organisations
  • Bilateral agencies
  • Governments
  • Donor institutions
  • Research organisations

This may require maintaining structured records, following institutional developments and synthesising information from multiple organisations or processes.

Convenings and Policy-Engagement Responsibilities

Research is only useful when it reaches the people making decisions. The Research Analyst will therefore contribute to workshops, roundtables and other policy-engagement activities.

Planning Events

The successful candidate will support the planning and organisation of:

  • Workshops
  • Roundtable discussions
  • Research launches
  • Partner meetings
  • Policy events
  • Stakeholder consultations

Responsibilities may include preparing timelines, maintaining participant lists, coordinating invitations and ensuring that logistical arrangements are completed.

Meeting Coordination

The role requires coordinating meetings among participants based in different countries and time zones.

The Research Analyst may need to:

  • Identify suitable time-zone options
  • Liaise with participants
  • Manage calendars
  • Confirm attendance
  • Circulate meeting materials
  • Maintain schedules
  • Follow up on agreed actions

Strong attention to detail is important because international coordination has a peculiar ability to turn one missing calendar invitation into a minor diplomatic incident.

Travel Arrangements

The Research Analyst will support travel planning for partners and participants attending Smart Buys Alliance events.

This may include coordinating itineraries, gathering traveller information and communicating logistical arrangements.

Required Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold a master’s degree in one of the following areas:

  • Economics
  • Public policy
  • International development
  • Development economics
  • A closely related discipline

The position requires advanced analytical training, particularly because the successful candidate will work with empirical research, quantitative methods and policy evidence.

Required Professional Experience

Candidates must have at least four years of professional experience in economic or public-policy analysis related to international development.

Relevant experience may have been gained in:

  • Policy research organisations
  • Universities
  • International organisations
  • Government institutions
  • Development agencies
  • Think tanks
  • Consulting organisations
  • NGOs
  • Philanthropic foundations

Applicants should demonstrate meaningful responsibility for analytical work rather than only general exposure to development projects.

Research and Quantitative Skills

Candidates must have strong research and quantitative analytical skills.

They should have experience designing and conducting empirical research in an academic or professional environment.

Expected capabilities include:

  • Structuring research questions
  • Reviewing relevant literature
  • Working with quantitative datasets
  • Cleaning and validating data
  • Applying appropriate analytical methods
  • Interpreting findings
  • Communicating limitations
  • Producing credible research outputs

Knowledge of causal-inference methods is required.

This may include familiarity with methods used to estimate the effects of programmes or policies and distinguish causal relationships from simple correlations.

Required and Desirable Software Skills

Applicants should be able to conduct quantitative analysis and produce visualisations using:

  • R
  • Stata

Experience with the following is an advantage:

  • Python
  • Git
  • Large language models
  • Textual-analysis tools
  • Evidence-synthesis methods

Candidates should explain how they have used relevant tools in actual research rather than merely listing software names in their CV.

Writing and Communication Skills

Excellent written communication is required.

The successful applicant must be able to summarise complicated empirical findings clearly and concisely for policy audiences.

Strong candidates will demonstrate the ability to:

  • Write logically structured research outputs
  • Explain quantitative findings in accessible language
  • Distinguish evidence from interpretation
  • Tailor writing to different audiences
  • Revise work in response to feedback
  • Maintain accuracy while remaining concise

Applicants must submit a writing sample, making the quality and relevance of that document particularly important.

Organisational and Coordination Experience

Candidates should have experience supporting:

  • Committees
  • Working groups
  • Research partnerships
  • Multi-stakeholder processes
  • Cross-institutional initiatives

Experience in professional communications, social-media management or event coordination is also relevant.

The role requires a person who can manage research responsibilities alongside operational tasks without allowing either side of the job to drift into chaos.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate:

  • High attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines
  • Strong calendar and scheduling skills
  • Experience maintaining shared documents
  • Clear and reliable communication
  • Ability to coordinate across institutions
  • Confidence working across time zones

Collaboration and Working Style

The Research Analyst will work with colleagues and partners from several institutions.

CGD is seeking someone with a collaborative and team-oriented working style who can contribute effectively across organisational boundaries.

The successful candidate should be able to:

  • Work independently when necessary
  • Seek guidance appropriately
  • Share information with colleagues
  • Respond constructively to feedback
  • Coordinate with external partners
  • Adapt to changing project priorities
  • Maintain professional relationships across institutions

Salary and Benefits

The annual salary range is:

£46,725–£51,187

The appointment also includes excellent benefits, although the vacancy information provided does not list the individual benefit components.

The exact salary offered within the range will likely depend on the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Contract Duration and Start Date

The successful candidate is expected to begin as soon as possible.

The position is fixed term and will run until:

29 February 2028

An extension may be possible if additional funding becomes available. Applicants should not assume that an extension is guaranteed.

London-Based Hybrid Working Arrangement

The position is based in London.

The successful candidate must live within commutable distance of CGD’s offices in the SW1 area and attend the office at least three days per week.

The position should therefore not be treated as a fully remote opportunity.

Applicants should consider the practical implications of commuting to central London before applying.

Right-to-Work Requirement

Candidates must already have, or be able to obtain, the legal right to live and work in the United Kingdom.

The vacancy does not state that visa sponsorship will be provided.

Applicants requiring sponsorship should confirm the organisation’s policy before relying on this position as a route to UK work authorisation.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates must submit:

  1. A current CV
  2. A cover letter
  3. A writing sample

Preparing the CV

The CV should clearly demonstrate:

  • Relevant academic qualifications
  • At least four years of applicable experience
  • Quantitative research responsibilities
  • Experience with R and Stata
  • Knowledge of causal-inference methods
  • Policy-writing experience
  • Coordination or event-management responsibilities

Preparing the Cover Letter

The cover letter should explain how the applicant meets the position’s requirements.

Candidates should provide specific examples of:

  • Empirical research they have conducted
  • Development-policy questions they have analysed
  • Datasets they have cleaned or managed
  • Quantitative methods they have applied
  • Research they have translated for policy audiences
  • Multi-stakeholder processes they have supported
  • Competing deadlines they have successfully managed

Selecting a Writing Sample

The writing sample should demonstrate the ability to communicate research clearly.

A strong sample may include:

  • A policy brief
  • A research report
  • An analytical blog
  • An academic paper section
  • A development-policy publication

Applicants should choose a sample that reflects their own contribution and is relevant to the role.

Manual Application Review

CGD states that applications will be reviewed manually.

No artificial-intelligence system or automated filter will be used to screen applicants.

Candidates should still tailor their materials carefully, but they do not need to construct their CV around an imaginary robot guarding the door with a keyword clipboard.

Equal Opportunity Statement

CGD Europe is an equal-opportunity employer committed to a collaborative, diverse and inclusive workplace.

Applicants will be considered without discrimination based on characteristics including:

  • Race
  • Colour
  • Creed
  • National origin
  • Ancestry
  • Gender
  • Gender identity or expression
  • Parental status
  • Veteran status
  • Marital status
  • Disability
  • Religious affiliation
  • Political affiliation
  • Age
  • Sexual orientation

Selection will be based on the requirements of the position and the applicant’s qualifications and experience.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST

Candidates should submit before the closing time to avoid last-minute technical problems.

International applicants should note that the deadline is stated in British Summer Time.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The CGD Research Analyst position offers an experienced international-development researcher the opportunity to contribute to influential work on cost-effectiveness and evidence use in development policy.

The role combines quantitative research, policy writing, large-scale textual analysis, coordination and stakeholder engagement. It is especially suited to candidates who can move confidently between data, ideas and the practical machinery of international collaboration.

Applicants need a relevant master’s degree, at least four years of professional experience, strong quantitative skills and experience using R and Stata. Knowledge of causal inference is required, while experience with Python, Git, evidence synthesis or large language models would strengthen an application.

The position is based in London, offers a salary of £46,725–£51,187, and will continue until 29 February 2028, with a possible extension depending on funding.

Qualified candidates must submit their CV, cover letter and writing sample by 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST.

item.content:encoded:
The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies 2026–2027 is now accepting applications for its prestigious fellowships and grants designed to strengthen and reshape the future of China studies across North America. Administered by the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) and generously supported by the Henry Luce Foundation, the program provides substantial funding, research support, mentorship opportunities, and professional development resources for graduate students, early-career scholars, and researchers working in China studies. As the academic landscape surrounding China continues to evolve, scholars increasingly face numerous challenges, including limited access to research materials, shrinking funding opportunities, geopolitical tensions, and barriers to academic collaboration. Recognizing these challenges, ACLS has redesigned the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies to better support researchers and ensure that China studies remains a vibrant, inclusive, and globally relevant field.

The program offers multiple funding opportunities ranging from travel grants to flexible and long-term fellowships, allowing scholars to pursue innovative research while contributing to public understanding of China, its history, cultures, societies, and global influence.

About the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies

Since its establishment in 2012, the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies has played an important role in supporting scholars throughout North America, particularly those in the early stages of their academic careers.

Following extensive consultations with researchers, universities, and stakeholders in 2023, ACLS redesigned the program to respond to the changing needs of the discipline. The new structure focuses not only on providing financial assistance but also on building stronger academic networks, expanding access to research resources, encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration, and fostering publicly engaged scholarship.

The program seeks to ensure that future generations of scholars have the resources, support systems, and institutional capacity necessary to produce meaningful research that benefits both academia and the broader public.

Program Objectives

The redesigned Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies is guided by three major goals:

1. Expand the Field of China Studies

The program seeks to broaden China studies by:

  • Supporting diverse scholarly voices
  • Encouraging new perspectives on Chinese history, society, and culture
  • Promoting scholarship from researchers with varied educational and professional backgrounds
  • Supporting institutions that have historically had fewer opportunities in the field

2. Build Sustainable Academic Infrastructure

The initiative aims to address long-term challenges affecting China studies by:

  • Building stronger scholarly networks
  • Supporting collaboration among researchers
  • Developing lasting academic infrastructure
  • Creating strategies that strengthen the future of the discipline

3. Promote Public Understanding

The program encourages research that helps the wider public better understand:

  • China’s history
  • Chinese cultures
  • Contemporary Chinese society
  • China’s influence on global communities
  • China’s impact on international politics, economics, and culture

Fellowship and Grant Opportunities Available for 2026–2027

Applicants may apply for several funding opportunities depending on their academic stage and research needs.

1. Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies

These grants support travel related to China studies research.

Grant Value

  • Up to $5,000

Duration

  • Travel may take place at any point during a 12-month period.

Intended Applicants

  • Graduate students
  • Non-tenure-track researchers

These grants are ideal for scholars who need to:

  • Visit archives
  • Conduct field research
  • Access specialized collections
  • Collaborate with other researchers
  • Participate in research-related activities

2. Flexible Early Career Fellowships

Designed specifically for scholars with demanding teaching or service responsibilities.

Fellowship Benefits

  • $15,000 stipend
  • No leave from employment is required

These fellowships allow recipients to:

  • Conduct research
  • Complete writing projects
  • Prepare journal articles
  • Develop books and manuscripts
  • Advance scholarly publications

This opportunity is particularly valuable for faculty members whose teaching or institutional duties make long-term research leave difficult.

3. Long-Term Early Career Fellowships

These fellowships provide significant support for scholars who need dedicated time for research.

Fellowship Duration

  • Four to nine months

Fellowship Funding

  • Minimum stipend: $20,000
  • Maximum stipend: $45,000

Recipients are expected to take full leave from university responsibilities in order to focus exclusively on research and writing leading toward a major scholarly publication.

Supported Academic Fields

The Luce/ACLS Program supports research in:

  • Humanities
  • Interpretive social sciences

Importantly:

  • There are no restrictions regarding research methodology.
  • There are no restrictions regarding historical time periods.

Researchers are encouraged to pursue innovative, interdisciplinary, and creative scholarship.

Publicly Engaged Scholarship

One of the defining features of the Luce/ACLS Program is its commitment to making academic knowledge accessible to wider audiences.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to design research projects that:

  • Inform public understanding
  • Increase public engagement with scholarship
  • Make humanistic knowledge more accessible
  • Demonstrate broader societal relevance

ACLS believes that scholarly knowledge should serve the public good rather than remain confined within academic institutions.

Mentorship and Professional Networking

Beyond financial support, fellows gain access to valuable networking opportunities.

The program hosts:

  • Mentorship activities
  • Professional networking events
  • Alumni engagement
  • Community-building opportunities

A networking and mentorship event will be organized alongside the Association for Asian Studies Annual Conference. Fellows selected for the 2026–2027 cohort will receive additional information in January 2027.

Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project

An important component of the program is the Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project.

This initiative seeks to improve scholarly access to important research materials by providing:

  • A directory of significant Sinophone collections located outside mainland China
  • A common access plan that helps researchers locate collections across participating institutions
  • Best-practice resources for digitizing and preserving print collections

The Digital Mapping Project strengthens research infrastructure while improving long-term access to valuable historical and cultural resources.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

The Luce/ACLS Program recognizes diversity as an essential component of academic excellence.

The program actively seeks applicants representing diverse:

  • Academic disciplines
  • Institutional affiliations
  • Educational backgrounds
  • Personal experiences
  • Research topics
  • Historical periods
  • Scholarly methodologies

Applications are welcomed without discrimination based on:

  • Race
  • Ethnicity
  • Gender
  • Sexual orientation
  • Religion
  • National origin
  • Disability
  • Age
  • Other personal identities

Selection is based solely on academic merit and program eligibility.

Benefits of the Luce/ACLS Program

Successful applicants will benefit from:

  • Funding of up to $45,000
  • Research support
  • Travel funding
  • Dedicated writing time
  • Professional mentorship
  • Academic networking opportunities
  • Participation in scholarly communities
  • Access to valuable research resources
  • Increased opportunities for publication
  • Enhanced professional development

Interested applicants should click HERE to apply by selecting a favourable term of their choice and learn more.

Application Deadline

The following competitions share the same application deadline:

  • Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Flexible
  • Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Long-Term
  • Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies

Application Deadline: November 5, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline and carefully review the eligibility requirements for their chosen competition.

Contact Information

Applicants seeking additional information should review the respective competition pages or contact the program through the ACLS China Studies office.

Institutional administrators, including Offices of Sponsored Projects, are also encouraged to consult the general guidance provided by ACLS regarding institutional application procedures.

Conclusion

The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies continues to serve as one of North America’s most significant funding initiatives for scholars studying China within the humanities and interpretive social sciences. Through its redesigned fellowships, grants, mentorship programs, and digital resource initiatives, ACLS is investing in the future of China studies by empowering researchers, promoting inclusive scholarship, and strengthening the academic infrastructure needed for long-term success. Whether you are a graduate student seeking travel support, an early-career academic balancing teaching responsibilities, or a recent PhD looking for dedicated research time, this program provides valuable financial assistance and professional opportunities to advance your scholarship. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and submit their applications before the November 5, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Women continue to play a vital role in driving economic growth, strengthening families, and building resilient communities. However, many women—particularly those living in underserved communities and women with disabilities—still face significant barriers to accessing finance, markets, productive resources, and leadership opportunities. Addressing these challenges requires targeted interventions that promote gender equality, economic inclusion, and sustainable development.

The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is one such initiative designed to empower women economically while transforming the systems that continue to limit their participation. Implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) as part of the Christian Aid Women Transforming Economies Signature Programme in Nigeria, THRIVE seeks to create lasting change by improving women’s access to dignified work, financial opportunities, entrepreneurship support, climate-resilient livelihoods, and decision-making processes.

This comprehensive 48-month initiative focuses on strengthening local economic systems so that women can thrive as entrepreneurs, farmers, business owners, and community leaders while promoting inclusive economic development.

About the THRIVE Project

The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is a four-year development initiative aimed at transforming local economies to become more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable for women.

The project recognizes that meaningful economic empowerment goes beyond providing financial support. It also requires changing the structures, relationships, policies, and social norms that prevent women from fully participating in economic activities.

Through collaboration with community stakeholders, financial institutions, women’s organizations, policymakers, and development partners, THRIVE seeks to build economic systems that value women’s contributions and ensure equal access to opportunities.

The project is funded by Christian Aid and implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) in Nigeria.

Project Duration

The THRIVE project will run for:

  • 48 months (4 years)

This extended implementation period allows for sustainable interventions, long-term capacity building, and measurable improvements in women’s economic participation and resilience.

Geographic Focus

The THRIVE project is currently being implemented in:

  • Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area (LGA)
  • Nasarawa State
  • Nigeria

Communities participating in the project are carefully selected through detailed assessments that consider:

  • Gender inclusion
  • Disability inclusion
  • Market accessibility
  • Community needs
  • Economic vulnerability

This approach ensures that resources reach women and communities with the greatest need.

The Challenges THRIVE Seeks to Address

Across many communities, women continue to face structural inequalities that prevent them from achieving economic independence.

THRIVE aims to address several key challenges, including:

Limited Access to Finance

Many women entrepreneurs and farmers struggle to obtain:

  • Business financing
  • Agricultural loans
  • Investment capital
  • Savings opportunities
  • Financial services

Without adequate financial support, expanding businesses or increasing productivity becomes extremely difficult.

Limited Access to Productive Assets

Women often have fewer opportunities to access essential productive resources such as:

  • Agricultural land
  • Modern farming tools
  • Equipment
  • Technology
  • Business infrastructure

These limitations reduce income generation and long-term economic growth.

Unsafe and Unequal Market Conditions

Many women operate within markets that present significant barriers, including:

  • Gender discrimination
  • Limited market access
  • Low bargaining power
  • Poor infrastructure
  • Unfair trading conditions

THRIVE seeks to improve women’s ability to participate in profitable and inclusive markets.

Unpaid Care Responsibilities

Women frequently shoulder unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities that reduce the time available for:

  • Business development
  • Skills training
  • Employment
  • Leadership
  • Economic participation

Reducing this burden is essential for achieving gender-equitable economies.

Limited Participation in Decision-Making

Women often have little influence over:

  • Local economic policies
  • Community planning
  • Market governance
  • Resource allocation
  • Development priorities

THRIVE supports women’s participation in leadership and policy discussions that directly affect their livelihoods.

Project Goal

The primary goal of THRIVE is to build gender-just economies where women enjoy:

  • Greater economic rights
  • Increased income security
  • Improved access to productive opportunities
  • Equal participation in markets
  • Stronger influence over economic policies
  • Sustainable and resilient livelihoods

Ultimately, the project seeks to transform local economic systems into environments where women can succeed without discrimination or structural barriers.

APPLY HERE

THRIVE’s Four Strategic Pillars

The project is built around four integrated intervention areas that work together to strengthen women’s economic empowerment.

1. Evidence for Change

THRIVE generates research and evidence on barriers affecting women to promote informed policy development.

Activities include:

  • Research on unpaid care work
  • Studies on disability inclusion
  • Gender analysis
  • Policy advocacy
  • Community consultations
  • Evidence-based recommendations

The information gathered helps shape more inclusive economic policies and practices.

2. Enterprise Development and Skills Building

The project equips women with practical knowledge and business skills needed for long-term success.

Support includes:

  • MSME coaching
  • Entrepreneurship development
  • Business management training
  • Digital literacy training
  • Enterprise growth support
  • Skills development for young women
  • Capacity building for women with disabilities

These interventions help women establish, strengthen, and expand their businesses.

3. Financial Inclusion and Market Access

Access to finance and profitable markets is critical for sustainable economic growth.

THRIVE strengthens women’s financial opportunities by:

  • Supporting Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs)
  • Connecting women with financial institutions
  • Improving access to capital
  • Facilitating market linkages
  • Expanding business networks
  • Strengthening value chains

These efforts enable women to grow sustainable enterprises and increase household incomes.

4. Climate Resilience

Climate change continues to threaten livelihoods, particularly for women working in agriculture.

THRIVE promotes climate-smart economic activities including:

  • Poultry production
  • Apiculture (beekeeping)
  • Dry-season gardening
  • Climate-resilient farming
  • Livelihood diversification
  • Sustainable agricultural practices

These initiatives help women adapt to climate change while improving food security and income generation.

Who Will Benefit?

The THRIVE project directly supports 300 women from various economic backgrounds.

Primary beneficiaries include:

  • Women-led Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
  • Aspiring women entrepreneurs
  • Women farmers
  • Agro-processors
  • Women with disabilities

The project prioritizes women facing economic exclusion and limited access to development opportunities.

Strategic Partnerships

Successful implementation of THRIVE relies on collaboration with multiple stakeholders.

Key partners include:

  • Christian Aid
  • Women Environmental Programme (WEP)
  • Women’s Rights Organisations (WROs)
  • Local policymakers
  • Financial institutions
  • Community leaders
  • Development partners

These partnerships strengthen implementation while ensuring sustainable community ownership.

Expected Impact

Through its integrated approach, THRIVE aims to deliver long-term outcomes including:

  • Increased economic independence for women
  • Improved entrepreneurship capacity
  • Greater financial inclusion
  • Enhanced market participation
  • Stronger climate resilience
  • Improved policy influence
  • Better livelihoods for women and families
  • Inclusive local economic development
  • Reduced gender inequality
  • Sustainable community growth

Why the THRIVE Project Matters

Women’s economic empowerment is one of the strongest drivers of sustainable development. When women have equal access to financial resources, education, entrepreneurship opportunities, and leadership positions, communities become more resilient, economies become stronger, and poverty declines.

The THRIVE project addresses not only individual economic challenges but also the systemic barriers that prevent women from fully participating in economic life. By investing in women entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, the project contributes to inclusive development while supporting broader goals of gender equality, climate resilience, and economic justice.

Its comprehensive model demonstrates how coordinated interventions across finance, skills development, policy, and climate adaptation can create lasting and transformative change.

Visit HERE to learn more about the THRIVE Project 2026

Conclusion

The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project represents a significant investment in women’s economic empowerment in Nigeria. Through entrepreneurship support, financial inclusion, climate-resilient livelihoods, policy advocacy, and capacity building, the project seeks to create lasting opportunities for women while transforming the local economic systems that shape their lives.

By directly supporting women-led enterprises, aspiring entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, THRIVE contributes to building more inclusive, resilient, and gender-just economies. As implementation continues over its 48-month duration, the project is expected to deliver meaningful improvements in livelihoods, economic participation, and sustainable community development across Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area.

item.content:encoded:
The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the British Academy have officially opened applications for the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027, a prestigious international research collaboration programme designed for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences. The symposium offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars from the United Kingdom and Germany to collaborate on pressing global issues surrounding the relationship between humans and nature while building long-term international research partnerships.

The symposium, scheduled to take place from 21–23 April 2027, will bring together approximately 30 outstanding early career researchers, with around 15 participants from the United Kingdom and 15 from Germany, creating an interdisciplinary platform for networking, intellectual exchange, and collaborative research.

In addition to fully covering participants’ travel-related expenses, the programme also provides opportunities to compete for seed funding to support future international collaborative research projects.

If you are an early career researcher passionate about sustainability, resilience, environmental justice, policy development, or the intersection between society and nature, this symposium presents an outstanding opportunity to connect with leading researchers and develop meaningful international collaborations.

About the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is a collaborative initiative jointly organized by the British Academy and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation.

The programme is specifically designed to strengthen research partnerships between scholars in the United Kingdom and Germany while encouraging interdisciplinary approaches to solving today’s most complex societal and environmental challenges.

The 2027 symposium will be held between:

  • Wednesday, 21 April 2027
  • Friday, 23 April 2027

Before the physical symposium begins, participants will also have opportunities to engage virtually by discussing research interests, exchanging ideas, and beginning collaborative conversations that can continue during and after the event.

Rather than functioning as a traditional academic conference, the symposium emphasizes interactive discussions, collaborative learning, networking, and the development of future joint research initiatives.

Symposium Theme

Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future

The 2027 edition focuses on the broad interdisciplinary theme:

“Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future.”

The organizers recognize that the relationship between humans and the natural environment has become one of the defining issues of the modern world.

Throughout history, there have been different perspectives regarding humanity’s place within nature.

Some viewpoints argue that humans possess the authority to manage and control nature, while others believe humans are an integral part of nature and should coexist with natural systems in more sustainable and balanced ways.

Today, increasing global crises—including climate change, biodiversity loss, technological transformation, economic pressures, environmental degradation, and population growth—have intensified the urgency of reconsidering this relationship.

The symposium aims to encourage participants to rethink how societies interact with ecological systems while identifying practical and innovative pathways toward greater resilience.

Research Topics

Participants are encouraged to explore a wide variety of interdisciplinary perspectives.

Potential discussion areas include, but are not limited to:

  • Contested understandings of society and nature
  • Human-nature conceptualizations
  • Environmental and social justice
  • Sustainability challenges
  • Ecological resilience
  • Coupled human-natural systems
  • Ethics and philosophy
  • Political dimensions of environmental governance
  • Economic approaches to sustainability
  • Geographical perspectives
  • Public policy development
  • Knowledge production
  • Narrative development
  • Artistic perspectives on environmental challenges
  • Interdisciplinary research approaches
  • Future resilience strategies

Researchers from diverse academic backgrounds are encouraged to contribute fresh perspectives and innovative ideas.

Objectives of the Symposium

The symposium has several important goals, including:

  • Strengthening collaboration between UK and German researchers.
  • Building long-term interdisciplinary research networks.
  • Encouraging innovative thinking across humanities and social sciences.
  • Promoting international academic partnerships.
  • Supporting future collaborative research initiatives.
  • Developing practical policy solutions for sustainability and resilience.
  • Encouraging knowledge sharing among early career scholars.
  • Providing networking opportunities with leading researchers.
  • Facilitating cross-disciplinary discussions on global challenges.

Symposium Format

Unlike conventional academic meetings, the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium prioritizes interaction and collaboration.

Participants can expect:

  • Interactive research discussions
  • Thematic sessions
  • Collaborative workshops
  • Networking activities
  • Group debates
  • Research idea exchanges
  • Collaborative planning sessions
  • Opportunities to establish future partnerships

The programme allocates substantial time for participants to build professional relationships and explore opportunities for future joint projects.

Seed Funding for Future Collaborations

One of the most attractive features of the symposium is the opportunity to apply for seed funding.

Participants will have the chance to develop collaborative research proposals during the symposium through a dedicated “sandpit” session held on the final day.

During this session, researchers will:

  • Form international research teams
  • Develop collaborative project ideas
  • Draft research proposals
  • Submit seed funding applications before the symposium concludes

Eligible collaborations may involve:

  • Bilateral partnerships
  • International research groups
  • Interdisciplinary collaborations

The organizers emphasize that funded collaborations must have an international composition.

Benefits of the Programme

Successful applicants will enjoy numerous benefits, including:

Fully Funded Participation

The symposium covers:

  • Travel costs
  • Accommodation
  • Visa expenses

Participants are therefore able to focus entirely on the academic programme without worrying about major travel-related costs.

International Networking

Participants will have the opportunity to:

  • Meet leading early career researchers.
  • Build long-lasting professional relationships.
  • Expand international academic networks.
  • Identify future collaborators.

Research Collaboration

Researchers will:

  • Share ongoing research.
  • Exchange innovative ideas.
  • Learn from scholars in different disciplines.
  • Develop interdisciplinary collaborations.

Career Development

The symposium supports career progression by helping participants:

  • Increase international research visibility.
  • Strengthen collaborative research experience.
  • Build competitive research portfolios.
  • Access future funding opportunities.

Opportunity to Secure Seed Funding

Participants may receive funding to continue collaborative research after the symposium through competitive seed funding proposals.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the following eligibility criteria:

  • Be an early career researcher.
  • Be affiliated with a research institution in either the United Kingdom or Germany.
  • Demonstrate strong research interest in the symposium theme.
  • Show commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration.
  • Demonstrate potential for career development through participation.

Applications will be evaluated based on:

  • Research interests
  • Relevance to the symposium theme
  • Commitment to interdisciplinary engagement
  • Career development potential

Application Process

Interested applicants must complete an online application through the Flexi-Grant® system.

Applicants are advised to carefully review the official scheme guidance before submitting their application.

Incorrectly completed applications may be declared ineligible.

Successful applicants are expected to:

  • Attend the entire symposium.
  • Travel on the designated dates determined by the organizers.

Successful candidates are expected to be notified by the end of November 2026.

Important Dates

Activity Date
Applications Open 28 July 2026
Application Deadline 16 September 2026 (17:25 BST)
Notification of Successful Applicants End of November 2026
Symposium Dates 21–23 April 2027
Earliest Start Date 21 April 2027

How to Apply

Applicants should:

  1. Read the official scheme guidance carefully.
  2. Prepare the required application materials.
  3. Complete the online application through Flexi-Grant®.
  4. Submit the application before the official deadline.
  5. Await notification from the organizers.

Late or incorrectly submitted applications will not be considered.

APPLY HERE

Contact Information

For further enquiries regarding the symposium, applicants may contact:

Email: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk

Why You Should Apply

The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is much more than an academic meeting.

It provides early career researchers with a unique opportunity to:

  • Develop international collaborations.
  • Gain interdisciplinary research experience.
  • Build professional networks across two leading research nations.
  • Engage with experts tackling some of today’s most urgent societal and environmental challenges.
  • Access future collaborative funding opportunities.
  • Advance their academic careers within an international research environment.

For researchers seeking meaningful international partnerships and opportunities to contribute to global conversations on sustainability and resilience, this symposium represents an exceptional platform.

Visit HERE for more information about the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027.

Deadline

Application Deadline: 16 September 2026 at 17:25 BST

Conclusion

The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 offer an outstanding opportunity for early-career researchers to engage in interdisciplinary discussions, establish international collaborations, and contribute to innovative solutions addressing the complex relationship between humans and nature. Through fully funded participation, extensive networking opportunities, and access to competitive seed funding, the symposium equips emerging scholars with the resources and connections needed to advance both their research and academic careers. Eligible researchers affiliated with institutions in the United Kingdom or Germany are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline and take advantage of this prestigious international programme.

For more global Conference opportunities, visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
The UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) has launched applications for its inaugural Youth Climate and Nature Panel, a groundbreaking initiative designed to ensure that young people’s voices play a central role in shaping the country’s climate and nature policies. The panel will bring together passionate young people from across the United Kingdom to provide advice, share insights, and contribute directly to government discussions on environmental issues.

As the UK continues its transition toward a net-zero future, the government recognizes the importance of involving younger generations in decision-making processes. Through this panel, selected participants will have the opportunity to influence policies that will impact their generation and future generations.

About the Youth Climate and Nature Panel

The Youth Climate and Nature Panel is a government-led initiative that seeks to strengthen collaboration between young people and policymakers. It aims to ensure that climate and nature policies reflect the ideas, experiences, and priorities of young people from diverse backgrounds across the UK.

The panel will consist of 15 young people, bringing together a wide range of experiences, perspectives, and regional representation.

Panel members will:

  • Provide insight and advice on climate and nature policies.
  • Help improve government engagement with young people.
  • Strengthen collaboration between different generations on environmental issues.
  • Amplify youth voices and inspire wider climate action across the United Kingdom.

This initiative forms part of the UK government’s commitment to ensuring that communities and young people benefit from the country’s transition to a sustainable and net-zero future.

Why You Should Apply

Being selected for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel offers a unique opportunity to contribute to national policymaking while developing valuable leadership and communication skills.

Benefits include:

  • Contributing directly to UK climate and nature policies.
  • Representing young people at the national level.
  • Engaging with government officials and policymakers.
  • Building leadership, teamwork, and communication skills.
  • Collaborating with other passionate young people from across the UK.
  • Helping shape future environmental initiatives.
  • Gaining valuable experience that can strengthen future education and career opportunities.

Click HERE to learn more about the UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026.

Who Can Apply?

The current application round is open to young people aged 16 to 18 who are based in the United Kingdom.

Applicants should:

  • Have a genuine interest in climate change and nature.
  • Be willing to share their ideas and experiences.
  • Be passionate about making a positive difference.
  • Be open to working collaboratively with people from different backgrounds.

No previous experience in environmental policy or government work is required. The panel is looking for diverse voices rather than technical experts.

Commitment to Diversity

The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero is committed to creating a panel that reflects the diversity of young people across the UK. Partner organizations are also helping identify candidates with different life experiences and perspectives to ensure broad representation.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official application form provided by the UK Government.

Applicants are encouraged to submit thoughtful responses that explain:

  • Why climate and nature matter to them.
  • How their experiences can contribute to the panel.
  • Why they want to help shape future government policies.

APPLY HERE.

Application Deadline

Deadline: Friday, 11 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid missing this opportunity.

Conclusion

The UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity for young people to influence national climate and environmental policies while developing leadership skills and representing the voices of their generation. By joining the panel, participants will contribute to meaningful discussions that support the UK’s journey toward a sustainable future. If you are passionate about climate action, nature conservation, and creating positive change, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact. Be sure to submit your application before 11 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Values Partnerships Fall Fellowship 2026, an exciting paid fellowship opportunity designed for emerging leaders who are passionate about working at the intersection of culture, marketing, communications, creativity, and social impact. This highly competitive fellowship provides participants with practical experience supporting real-world campaigns, strategic partnerships, and community engagement initiatives while working alongside experienced professionals in one of the United States’ leading cultural marketing and social impact agencies.

The fellowship will run from September 9 to December 18, 2026, offering selected fellows an opportunity to gain hands-on experience working on projects for corporate organizations, nonprofits, entertainment companies, advocacy groups, and institutions committed to creating meaningful social impact.

Whether you are a university student, recent graduate, career changer, or an emerging professional interested in cultural strategy and purpose-driven work, this fellowship provides an excellent platform to build professional experience while contributing to projects that positively influence communities.

About Values Partnerships

Values Partnerships (VPI) is a nationally recognized marketing, communications, social impact, and insights agency based in the United States. For more than a decade, the organization has helped leading brands, institutions, nonprofits, and entertainment companies understand, engage, and empower what it calls the “New Majority”—including Generation Z, Generation Alpha, and multicultural communities.

The organization specializes in creating culturally relevant strategies that enable organizations to build authentic relationships with diverse audiences while driving measurable social and business impact.

Its work combines research, storytelling, creative communications, strategic partnerships, and community engagement to help clients connect with communities in meaningful ways.

What Values Partnerships Does

The agency collaborates with organizations to:

  • Build trust with communities
  • Design culturally relevant marketing campaigns
  • Develop creative engagement strategies
  • Launch purpose-driven partnerships
  • Produce community-centered events

  • Strengthen audience engagement
  • Deliver strategic communications

Over the years, Values Partnerships has established itself as a leader in helping organizations navigate culture, diversity, creativity, and social responsibility.

Rather than working on hypothetical assignments, fellows contribute directly to ongoing projects serving a wide variety of clients across different industries.

item.content:encoded:
Housing affordability continues to be one of the most pressing challenges facing cities across the globe. Municipal governments are increasingly seeking innovative strategies to improve access to affordable housing, strengthen urban planning, and develop sustainable communities. Bloomberg Philanthropies is addressing these challenges by recruiting talented professionals to support city governments through its Bloomberg Associates program.

Applications are now open for the Bloomberg Associates Housing Fellow position, a unique opportunity for professionals passionate about housing policy, urban development, sustainability, and public sector innovation. The fellowship offers the chance to work with leading municipal governments, contribute to strategic housing initiatives, and help improve the quality of life for communities through evidence-based policy development.

The position is fully remote, part-time, and offered on a six-month contract, making it suitable for professionals seeking meaningful consulting experience while maintaining flexibility.

About Bloomberg Philanthropies

Bloomberg Philanthropies is one of the world’s leading philanthropic organizations dedicated to improving lives through innovative solutions and strategic investments. Its work focuses on five major priority areas:

  • Arts and culture
  • Education
  • Environment
  • Government innovation
  • Public health

The organization’s mission is to help people live better and longer lives by creating lasting, catalytic change in communities around the world. Its approach combines innovation, practical experience, and partnerships with governments to solve complex public challenges.

About Bloomberg Associates

Bloomberg Associates serves as Bloomberg Philanthropies’ pro bono consulting arm. Founded by Michael R. Bloomberg, former Mayor of New York City and Founder of Bloomberg LP, the organization partners directly with city governments to improve public services and urban management.

The consulting teams support municipalities across nine major practice areas:

  • Cultural Assets Management
  • Marketing & Communications
  • Media and Digital Strategies
  • Municipal Integrity
  • Social Services
  • Sustainability
  • Transportation
  • Economic Development
  • Urban Planning

Within its Sustainability Practice, the Housing Team works alongside client cities to improve housing affordability and strengthen municipal housing systems through strategic planning, policy development, and technical assistance.

About the Housing Fellow Position

The Housing Fellow will become part of Bloomberg Associates’ Sustainability Practice and contribute to multiple housing projects serving different cities.

The successful fellow will collaborate with municipal governments on initiatives designed to increase housing affordability, improve housing programs, and support evidence-based decision-making.

This role provides exposure to public policy, strategic consulting, urban planning, housing research, and municipal governance while working alongside experienced professionals.

The fellowship is:

  • Remote
  • Part-time
  • Approximately 20 hours per week
  • Six-month contractual engagement

Key Responsibilities

The selected fellow will contribute to a broad range of housing initiatives, including:

Conduct Housing Program Research

Responsibilities include:

  • Reviewing existing municipal housing programs.
  • Conducting housing policy research.
  • Interviewing municipal staff.
  • Supporting housing program audits.

Develop Housing Needs Assessments

The fellow will assist cities by:

  • Producing detailed housing data analyses.
  • Managing consultants and project timelines.
  • Preparing reports and presentations.
  • Supporting comprehensive housing needs assessments.

Strengthen Housing Data Systems

Successful candidates will help municipalities:

  • Build public-facing housing dashboards.
  • Improve backend housing data infrastructure.
  • Develop standard operating procedures.
  • Support technical implementation across multiple cities.

Analyze Municipal Housing Programs

Responsibilities include:

  • Measuring program effectiveness.
  • Evaluating housing initiatives.
  • Producing analytical reports.
  • Creating executive-level presentations.

Research Housing Best Practices

The fellow will:

  • Study successful housing policies from other municipalities.
  • Produce case studies.
  • Recommend innovative approaches for local governments.
  • Support strategic housing policy development.

Stakeholder Coordination

The position also involves:

  • Coordinating with municipal officials.
  • Maintaining professional relationships.
  • Supporting project communication.
  • Working across multidisciplinary teams.

Required Qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate a combination of academic achievement, technical expertise, and professional experience.

Minimum requirements include:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline.
  • At least two years of professional experience.
  • Background in affordable housing, urban planning, or public/non-profit administration.
  • Strong analytical thinking.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Proven project execution experience.
  • Policy research experience.
  • Project management skills.
  • Strong interpersonal communication.
  • Excellent writing ability.
  • Presentation development skills.
  • Ability to explain complex data clearly.
  • Tableau knowledge (preferred).
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Strong organizational skills.
  • Professionalism when working with senior stakeholders.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Ability to quickly learn new subject matter.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This fellowship offers numerous professional development advantages.

Participants will have the opportunity to:

  • Work directly with city governments.
  • Influence housing affordability initiatives.
  • Gain consulting experience within Bloomberg Philanthropies.
  • Strengthen public policy and urban planning expertise.
  • Build project management skills.
  • Expand research and analytical capabilities.
  • Work remotely with flexible scheduling.
  • Contribute to high-impact municipal projects.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary professionals.
  • Develop expertise in housing strategy and sustainability.

Visit HERE for more information about the Bloomberg Associates Housing Fellow (Remote, Part-Time).

Remote Work Arrangement

The fellowship offers considerable flexibility.

Working conditions include:

  • Fully remote work.
  • Approximately 20 hours weekly.
  • Six-month contract.
  • Collaboration with multiple client cities.
  • Flexible project-based assignments.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Bloomberg Philanthropies is committed to creating an inclusive workplace and provides equal employment opportunities without discrimination based on legally protected characteristics.

The organization also provides reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities who require adjustments during the application process.

Salary

The posted hourly compensation ranges between:

US$26–US$35 per hour

Actual compensation may vary depending on factors such as geographic location, professional experience, education, training, market conditions, and skill level.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should prepare:

  • Updated résumé/CV.
  • Cover letter.
  • LinkedIn profile (optional but encouraged).
  • Information regarding work authorization.
  • Responses to employment eligibility questions.

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible since no closing date has been announced and recruitment may close once the position is filled.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Bloomberg Associates Housing Fellow position presents an outstanding opportunity for professionals who are passionate about affordable housing, municipal governance, and sustainable urban development. Through this remote fellowship, successful candidates will work alongside city governments to address housing affordability challenges using research, policy analysis, strategic planning, and data-driven solutions.

Whether your background is in urban planning, housing policy, public administration, or sustainability, this role offers valuable experience within one of the world’s leading philanthropic organizations. Professionals seeking to make a tangible impact on cities while advancing their careers in public policy and municipal consulting should strongly consider applying. With no published application deadline, interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible.

For more global Job opportunities, visit OFY HERE
