item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming industries, economies, and societies around the world. As AI systems become increasingly capable, ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and aligned with human values has become one of the most important scientific challenges of our time. To address these pressing concerns, AIXI Labs is inviting applications for its Research Fellowship, a prestigious opportunity designed for talented researchers interested in advancing the field of AI safety through rigorous theoretical and empirical research.

The AIXI Labs Research Fellowship offers participants the opportunity to work alongside some of the world’s leading AI safety researchers while receiving a monthly stipend ranging from £2,000 to £3,500, a dedicated machine learning compute budget, close mentorship, and the flexibility to work fully remotely from anywhere in the world or from the organization’s headquarters in London, United Kingdom.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, making this an excellent opportunity for aspiring AI researchers to join an internationally recognized research community focused on reducing existential risks from advanced artificial intelligence.

About AIXI Labs

AIXI Labs is a London-based nonprofit research organization dedicated to advancing AI safety through the lens of Algorithmic Information Theory (AIT).

Unlike many organizations that either focus exclusively on abstract mathematical models or highly practical machine learning systems that are difficult to analyze theoretically, AIXI Labs occupies a unique position by combining both rigorous theory and practical applications.

The organization’s research focuses on developing methods that are:

  • General enough to describe highly capable intelligent agents
  • Mathematically rigorous enough to produce provable safety guarantees
  • Applicable to modern Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI agents

The research agenda is built around AIXI, a well-known theoretical model of unbounded artificial superintelligence developed to study idealized intelligent agents. Researchers at AIXI Labs aim to translate theoretical breakthroughs into practical safety techniques applicable to modern AI systems.

About the AIXI Labs Research Fellowship

The AIXI Labs Research Fellowship is a quarterly rolling fellowship program created for researchers who want to make meaningful contributions to AI safety research.

Participants spend approximately one academic quarter working on a focused research project under the guidance of experienced mentors while collaborating with a growing international AI safety community.

The fellowship is designed to support independent researchers who wish to explore foundational questions while maintaining enough flexibility to pursue topics aligned with their own expertise and interests.

Fellowship Highlights

Selected fellows will receive:

  • Monthly stipend between £2,000 and £3,500
  • Dedicated machine learning compute budget
  • Close mentorship from leading AI researchers
  • Flexible remote work from anywhere in the world
  • Optional opportunity to work from London headquarters
  • Opportunity to publish research papers and technical articles
  • Access to one of the world’s emerging AI safety research communities
  • Potential renewal for exceptional fellows

Fellowship Duration

The fellowship runs on a quarterly basis, with each fellowship lasting approximately one academic quarter.

Applications are reviewed continuously throughout the year under a rolling admissions process.

Exceptional participants may be invited to extend or renew their fellowship.

Fellowship Location

Applicants may choose either of the following work arrangements:

  • Fully Remote (Worldwide)
  • London, United Kingdom

Researchers can participate from any country while collaborating virtually with mentors and fellow researchers.

Financial Support

Successful fellows receive substantial financial support throughout the program.

This includes:

  • Monthly stipend between £2,000 and £3,500
  • Dedicated compute budget for AI and machine learning experiments

The compute budget enables fellows to perform computationally intensive machine learning research without bearing personal infrastructure costs.

Research Mentorship

One of the strongest aspects of the fellowship is direct mentorship from AIXI Labs’ core research leadership.

Fellows work closely with:

  • Cole Wyeth — Founder & Executive Director
  • Marcus Hutter — Research Director
  • Aram Ebtekar — Founding Research Scientist

This close supervision provides participants with valuable guidance while allowing them to maintain ownership over their research projects.

Research Focus Areas

The fellowship supports projects across a broad range of AI safety topics grounded in algorithmic information theory.

Potential research directions include:

1. AI Safety Theory

Developing mathematical foundations for understanding safe intelligent agents.

2. Algorithmic Information Theory

Applying information-theoretic approaches to model intelligence and alignment.

3. Reinforcement Learning

Exploring safer reinforcement learning systems and decision-making agents.

4. Large Language Models

Studying the safety, behavior, and alignment of LLM-based agents.

5. AI Alignment

Investigating methods for aligning advanced AI systems with human goals.

6. Empirical AI Safety

Testing theoretical ideas using practical machine learning experiments.

Responsibilities of Fellows

Participants are expected to pursue a self-directed research agenda aligned with AIXI Labs’ mission.

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Conduct original AI safety research
  • Design and execute independent research projects
  • Align research with algorithmic-information-theoretic approaches
  • Perform empirical experiments where applicable
  • Produce high-quality written research outputs
  • Publish papers, technical reports, or blog posts
  • Communicate findings to the AI safety and machine learning communities

Researchers are encouraged to tailor their projects according to their own strengths and academic interests.

Minimum Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should demonstrate strong academic preparation in quantitative disciplines.

Minimum qualifications include:

  • Research background equivalent to a current PhD student
  • Alternatively, applicants with master’s-level mathematical expertise combined with substantial industry or applied research experience may also qualify for primarily empirical projects
  • Strong knowledge of:
    • Probability
    • Statistics
    • Information Theory
    • Reinforcement Learning
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong interest in reducing existential risks associated with advanced AI
  • Enthusiasm for AI safety research

Importantly, prior experience with AIXI or Algorithmic Information Theory is not required.

Preferred Qualifications

While not mandatory, competitive applicants may possess one or more of the following:

  • Publications at leading AI conferences such as:
    • NeurIPS
    • ICML
    • ICLR
    • ALT
    • COLT
  • Background in:
    • Algorithmic Information Theory
    • Computability Theory
    • Learning Theory
    • Theoretical Computer Science
  • Experience:
    • Fine-tuning Large Language Models
    • Evaluating LLMs
    • Red-teaming AI systems
    • Reinforcement Learning agents
  • Previous involvement with:
    • UAI community
    • AIXI community
    • Related reading groups

AIXI Labs emphasizes the quality and impact of an applicant’s strongest research contributions over the sheer number of publications.

Click HERE to read more.

Why Apply for the AIXI Labs Research Fellowship?

This fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity for researchers seeking to work on one of the most important scientific challenges of the coming decades.

Benefits include:

  • Competitive monthly financial support
  • Fully remote participation
  • Flexible project selection
  • Direct mentorship from internationally respected AI researchers
  • Dedicated compute resources
  • Opportunity to contribute to frontier AI safety research
  • Collaboration with an international research community
  • Potential fellowship renewal

Rolling Applications

Unlike programs with fixed annual deadlines, the AIXI Labs Research Fellowship reviews applications throughout the year.

This rolling admissions model allows qualified researchers to apply whenever they are ready, increasing accessibility for applicants worldwide.

Previous applicants remain eligible to apply for future fellowship rounds.

Deadline: There is no fixed application deadline. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis throughout the year.

Who Should Apply?

The fellowship is particularly suited for:

  • PhD students
  • Early-career AI researchers
  • Machine learning researchers
  • Reinforcement learning researchers
  • Computer scientists
  • Mathematicians
  • Statisticians
  • AI alignment researchers
  • Theoretical computer scientists
  • Researchers interested in AI existential risk

Candidates with strong mathematical backgrounds and a genuine passion for advancing AI safety will benefit most from this opportunity.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The AIXI Labs Research Fellowship represents an outstanding opportunity for researchers who want to contribute to one of the world’s most significant scientific and technological challenges: ensuring the safe development of advanced artificial intelligence.

By combining generous financial support, flexible remote participation, dedicated mentorship, computational resources, and access to a vibrant AI safety research community, the fellowship enables participants to pursue cutting-edge research with real-world impact. Whether your interests lie in theoretical AI, reinforcement learning, algorithmic information theory, or large language model safety, this fellowship provides an ideal environment to deepen your expertise while contributing to the future of responsible AI.

item.content:encoded:
City Bureau is accepting applications for its Fall 2026 Civic Information Fellowship, a paid, six-month professional development and community engagement program designed for people interested in journalism, civic participation, storytelling, public policy and community organizing.

The fellowship provides participants with practical training, individualized coaching and hands-on experience in identifying and addressing the information needs of Chicago communities. Fellows will work alongside City Bureau staff and other cohort members to research civic issues, engage with residents and create projects that help people access and use important local information.

The Fall 2026 fellowship cycle is scheduled to begin on September 8, 2026. Applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on August 11, 2026. City Bureau has stated that late applications will not be accepted. About City Bureau

City Bureau is a Chicago-based civic media laboratory that develops people-powered journalism practices and supports their adoption in communities across the United States.

The organization envisions communities in which people have access to the information, resources and tools they need to make informed decisions, shape their futures and participate meaningfully in democratic and civic life.

City Bureau’s work is rooted in the belief that local journalism should strengthen relationships, expand access to information, recognize community knowledge and contribute to a more equitable and participatory democracy. The organization was founded in Chicago and continues to place significant emphasis on the experiences, histories and information needs of communities across the city. About the City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship

The Civic Information Fellowship is a paid, two-phase program lasting approximately six months. It is intended for Chicago-area residents who want to develop their capabilities in:

  • Community engagement
  • Civic participation
  • Community-centered journalism
  • Public-interest storytelling
  • Research and interviewing
  • Local government and public policy
  • Information distribution
  • Audience engagement
  • Project development
  • Professional communication

With guidance from City Bureau staff, fellows will work individually and collaboratively to understand the information needs of Chicago communities. They will then design and implement projects that make useful civic information more accessible to residents.

The program gives particular attention to Chicago’s South and West sides. Fellows will be expected to spend meaningful time engaging with communities, building relationships, gathering information and understanding how residents create, receive and share information.

Participants will also examine how people engage with public institutions and participate in civic life. The fellowship encourages fellows to think creatively about improving local information systems, especially within Chicago’s communities of color. Purpose of the Fellowship

The fellowship is not limited to conventional newsroom reporting. Its broader purpose is to help participants understand how information affects community participation, government accountability and residents’ ability to navigate important public systems.

During the program, fellows will explore questions such as:

  • What information do community members need?
  • What prevents people from accessing reliable information?
  • Which public systems or civic processes are difficult to understand?
  • How can journalists and community organizations build stronger relationships with residents?
  • What formats are most effective for sharing information with different audiences?
  • How can information be distributed to the people who need it most?
  • How can residents use information to make decisions or hold institutions accountable?

Fellows will use their findings to design practical information-needs projects that respond to issues identified through community engagement.

What Selected Fellows Will Do

Participants will complete a combination of workshops, team meetings, community assignments, research activities, reflective exercises and project-development work.

1. Attend weekly workshops

Fellows will participate in weekly learning sessions led by City Bureau staff members and invited speakers. These workshops will cover topics related to journalism, civic life, community engagement, storytelling and project implementation.

2. Participate in weekly team meetings

Participants will meet regularly with City Bureau’s Civic Information and Engagement team. These meetings will provide opportunities to discuss assignments, review progress, address challenges and receive guidance.

3. Work collaboratively

Each fellow will work in a hands-on learning environment with City Bureau staff and five other fellowship participants.

Collaboration will be central to the experience. Fellows will share ideas, provide feedback, support one another’s projects and collectively examine Chicago’s information ecosystem.

4. Build journalism skills

The journalism component may include training and practical experience in:

  • Storytelling
  • Writing for different platforms and audiences
  • Research
  • Information gathering
  • Interviewing techniques
  • Journalism ethics
  • Accountability reporting
  • Explainer writing
  • Social video production
  • Public-interest communication

The program is designed to help participants communicate complex civic issues in formats that community members can understand and use.

5. Develop community-engagement skills

Fellows will learn how to establish meaningful and non-transactional relationships with residents and community partners.

Training and assignments may include:

  • Community relationship-building
  • Collaboration with local organizations
  • Community asset mapping
  • Conducting surveys
  • Identifying community resources
  • Understanding local information networks
  • Examining how residents receive and share information

City Bureau’s approach treats community engagement as a core part of journalism rather than as a temporary outreach activity. The organization emphasizes long-term relationships, shared learning and respect for the knowledge and resources that already exist within communities. 6. Strengthen civic-participation knowledge

Participants will improve their understanding of how Chicago’s government and public institutions operate.

This may involve:

  • Learning how city government works
  • Researching public policy
  • Attending and covering public meetings
  • Identifying responsible government officials
  • Understanding public decision-making structures
  • Examining government accountability
  • Learning how residents can participate in civic processes

7. Maintain weekly journals

Fellows will keep written or audio journals throughout the program. These journals will be used to document progress, reflect on lessons learned and evaluate personal and project development.

8. Produce public-facing content

Participants will create content related to their fellowship work and selected civic issues. This content may include:

  • Social media videos
  • Blog posts
  • Explainer articles
  • Community information resources
  • Project updates
  • Stories about civic governance
  • Content explaining public infrastructure or government systems

9. Design an information-needs project

One of the fellowship’s central responsibilities will be the development of a project that addresses a community information need.

Fellows will spend time engaging with residents, identifying information gaps and developing a project capable of responding to a specific issue.

Projects may use different formats depending on the community need, target audience and information being communicated.

10. Develop distribution strategies

Producing information will only be one part of the project. Fellows will also be expected to determine how that information can reach the people who need it.

Participants will develop distribution and audience-engagement strategies to ensure that their work is accessible, relevant and actionable.

The goal is to create information that people can apply in their daily lives rather than content that is simply published without a clear distribution plan.

11. Receive coaching and professional development

City Bureau staff and editors will provide fellows with one-on-one feedback and additional coaching.

The program will also support participants in areas such as:

  • Career development
  • Professional goal-setting
  • Accountability
  • Time management
  • Project planning
  • Identifying professional strengths
  • Meeting personal and program objectives

12. Promote completed work

Fellows will have opportunities to share their projects through City Bureau’s networks and community partnerships. This can help participants develop a professional portfolio, strengthen community relationships and expand the reach of their work. Fellowship Structure

The City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship is divided into two phases. Each phase has different objectives, working hours and payment arrangements.

Phase One: Community Research and Project Design

During the first phase, fellows will focus on spending time within communities and understanding residents’ information needs.

Participants will conduct research, engage with community members, map local resources and begin designing a project that responds to an identified information gap.

Phase One duration

Phase One will last 14 weeks.

Phase One time commitment

Fellows must complete approximately 12 hours of work each week.

The weekly schedule will generally include:

  • A two-hour learning session on Monday or Tuesday
  • A four-hour in-person meeting and co-working session on Wednesday
  • Six flexible hours for independent and community-based work

Monday or Tuesday learning sessions will normally be conducted through Zoom during evening hours. City Bureau will work with selected fellows to identify a suitable meeting time. Some sessions may occasionally be held in person.

Wednesday sessions will be held at City Bureau’s Bronzeville office. Fellows will attend either from noon to 4 p.m. or from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. These sessions will include meetings with City Bureau staff and co-working time with the fellowship group. Lunch will be provided.

The remaining six hours may be scheduled more flexibly. Fellows will use this time for activities such as:

  • Community engagement
  • Research and information gathering
  • Interviews
  • Community mapping
  • Writing
  • Fellowship assignments
  • Journaling
  • Communication with team members

Phase One stipend

Participants will receive a stipend of $5,000 for completing Phase One. Payments will be issued in two-week increments.

Phase One attendance requirements

Required sessions are mandatory. Fellows may miss up to four required sessions during the 14-week period.

Any missed time must be completed during surrounding weeks. Failure to meet the attendance and participation requirements may affect a fellow’s ability to complete the program. Phase Two: Project Implementation

Fellows who successfully complete Phase One will be invited to continue into Phase Two.

During this stage, participants will move from research and project design to implementation. They will carry out the information-needs projects developed during the first phase and receive continuing support from City Bureau teams.

Phase Two duration

Phase Two will last 10 weeks.

Phase Two time commitment

Participants must complete approximately eight hours of work each week.

The schedule will include:

  • One two-hour virtual learning session focused on an advanced skill
  • One two-hour in-person co-working session with fellows and City Bureau staff
  • Four flexible hours for implementing project activities

The flexible working time may be used for completing project tasks, producing information resources, engaging with communities and receiving support from City Bureau’s Civic Information and Engagement and Chicago Documenters teams.

Phase Two stipend

Participants will receive a stipend of $2,800 during Phase Two. Payments will be distributed in two-week increments.

Fellows who complete both phases may therefore receive a combined stipend of up to $7,800.

Phase Two attendance requirements

The Phase Two time commitment is mandatory. Fellows may miss up to three required sessions during the 10-week period and must make up the missed time during adjacent weeks. Important Participation Requirements

Applicants do not need a particular professional qualification or a formal journalism background.

City Bureau is interested in people who have demonstrated engagement with civic issues, journalism, public policy, community work or organizing. This experience may have been developed through:

  • Personal initiatives
  • Community projects
  • Volunteer work
  • Educational programs
  • Professional training
  • School activities
  • Internships
  • Journalism projects
  • Chicago Documenters participation
  • Direct lived experience

Applicants should be interested in storytelling, community-building, civic information and finding creative ways to connect people with important information.

Former City Bureau fellows are permitted to apply.

Because the fellowship includes substantial in-person engagement, applicants must live in Chicago or the surrounding area. City Bureau does not offer a fully remote participation option.

Participants must have reliable transportation to City Bureau’s Bronzeville office and to neighborhoods across Chicago’s South and West sides. Applicants must also be legally authorized to work in the United States.

City Bureau particularly values applicants with lived or professional experience on Chicago’s South and West sides. Active and experienced Chicago Documenters are also strongly valued.

The organization cautions full-time students about applying because of the program’s significant weekly workload. Exceptions may occasionally be considered for students who can demonstrate that they are capable of managing multiple time commitments effectively. Who Would Be a Strong Candidate?

A strong applicant may be someone who:

  • Regularly asks questions about how public institutions operate
  • Cares about local civic issues
  • Wants to improve access to community information
  • Enjoys interviewing and listening to people
  • Is interested in journalism or public-interest communication
  • Has participated in community initiatives
  • Understands issues affecting Chicago neighborhoods
  • Wants to learn about public policy and local government
  • Can collaborate effectively with a small team
  • Is comfortable receiving feedback
  • Can manage mandatory weekly commitments
  • Is interested in designing practical community projects
  • Values racial equity and community-centered journalism
  • Can travel to different Chicago neighborhoods

Professional journalism experience may be helpful, but it is not mandatory. City Bureau is primarily looking for applicants who demonstrate curiosity, commitment, reliability and a genuine interest in community information.

Mandatory In-Person Participation

Applicants should carefully consider the in-person requirements before submitting an application.

The fellowship requires participants to:

  • Attend Wednesday meetings at the Bronzeville office
  • Travel throughout Chicago’s South and West Side neighborhoods
  • Conduct direct community engagement
  • Complete local interviews and assignments
  • Participate in in-person co-working sessions
  • Maintain regular attendance

Repeated absences may place a fellow’s completion of the program at risk. Applicants should therefore confirm that their employment, education, family responsibilities and transportation arrangements will allow them to meet the required schedule. Important Policy on Artificial Intelligence

City Bureau has explicitly instructed applicants not to use artificial intelligence to complete their fellowship applications.

The selection team wants applicants to communicate their own ideas, experiences and perspectives. Using AI-generated content in an application may result in disqualification.

Applicants should therefore write their application responses independently and ensure that the submitted material authentically reflects their personal voice, lived experience and reasons for applying. Optional Fellowship Webinar and Question-and-Answer Session

  3. Consider whether they can complete the required weekly working hours.
  4. Confirm that they can travel to the Bronzeville office and other Chicago neighborhoods.
  5. Review the two-phase structure and attendance requirements.
  6. Prepare original responses based on their own experiences.
  7. Submit the application before the deadline.
  8. Avoid using artificial intelligence to draft or complete application answers.

Selected fellows will have the opportunity to identify an important community information need and develop a practical project that helps Chicago residents understand and navigate civic issues.
